explanation: The name refers to its layers: puff pastry, rolled and folded, holds hundreds of butter-thin sheets, and three sheets of it are stacked with pastry cream.

claims.text: Mille-feuille means 'a thousand leaves' in French, after its many layers.
Mille-feuille is not named after a thousand years, a baker or a town in Normandy.
Puff pastry made by repeated rolling and folding holds hundreds of thin layers.
A classic mille-feuille stacks three layers of puff pastry with pastry cream between them.
